citerne_page.name: Portuguese Cistern
citerne_page.hero_subtitle: Vaulted underground reservoir with a single shaft of light on still water — El Jadida’s most atmospheric room.
citerne_page.overview.title: Light on still water
citerne_page.overview.p1: The Portuguese Cistern is a vaulted underground chamber built in the 16th century. A circular opening in the ceiling drops a beam of daylight onto shallow water — the image that defines El Jadida for many visitors.
citerne_page.overview.p2: Go early if you can: fewer people and clearer reflections. The space is compact; twenty to forty minutes inside is enough for most visitors, longer if you wait for a quiet frame.
citerne_page.overview.p3: It sits inside the UNESCO Portuguese City, so combine it with the ramparts and Bastion of the Angel on the same morning.

citerne_page.faq.title: Portuguese Cistern FAQ
citerne_page.faq.q1.question: Is there an entry fee?
citerne_page.faq.q1.answer: Yes, a small ticket is required. Keep small change ready.
citerne_page.faq.q2.question: Best time of day?
citerne_page.faq.q2.answer: Morning for softer light and fewer groups; midday gives a stronger vertical beam.
citerne_page.faq.q3.question: How long inside?
citerne_page.faq.q4.question: Photography allowed?
citerne_page.faq.q4.answer: Usually yes — be respectful of other visitors and any posted rules.
citerne_page.faq.q5.question: Combine with the ramparts?
citerne_page.faq.q5.answer: Yes. The cistern and walls form the core Portuguese circuit.
